name: Transformer
what: Encoder–decoder built only from attention and feed-forward layers.

name: GPT-1
what: Decoder-only transformer pre-trained on books, then fine-tuned; 12 layers, d = 768.

name: BERT
what: Encoder-only, bidirectional, pre-trained by masked-token prediction.

name: GPT-2
what: Decoder-only at 1.5B parameters; LayerNorm moved to the input of each sublayer (Pre-LN) plus a final LayerNorm.

name: T5
what: Systematic comparison of encoder–decoder, decoder-only and prefix LM; encoder–decoder with denoising won at the time.

name: GPT-3
what: 175B parameters (96 layers, d = 12,288, 96 heads); alternates dense and banded sparse attention.

name: Relative positions
what: Learned embeddings of clipped relative distance added to keys and values (Shaw, Uszkoreit, Vaswani).

name: Transformer-XL
what: Segment-level recurrence with relative sinusoidal encoding.

name: T5 relative bias
what: A learned scalar per head added to each score, by log-spaced distance bucket (32 buckets up to 128).

name: RoPE
what: Rotate query and key pairs by mθᵢ, θᵢ = 10000^(−2i/d); scores depend only on relative position.
used: PaLM, LLaMA and nearly every decoder LLM since

name: ALiBi
what: No position embeddings; add −m·(i−j) to scores with fixed per-head slopes m = 2^(−8k/h).

name: NoPE
what: Decoder-only models with no position encoding at all generalise to longer inputs better on some tasks.

name: Position interpolation
what: Squeeze positions by L/L′ to extend RoPE context; LLaMA to 32k in ~1,000 steps.

name: YaRN
what: Interpolate only the low-frequency RoPE dimensions and add an attention temperature 0.1 ln s + 1.

name: LongRoPE
what: Search for non-uniform per-dimension RoPE rescaling; context beyond 2M tokens.

name: RMSNorm
what: LayerNorm without mean-centring: x / RMS(x) · g.
used: LLaMA, Llama 3, Mistral, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3, gpt-oss, Gemma

name: Pre-LN analysis
what: Shows Post-LN has large gradients near the output at initialisation, hence warm-up; Pre-LN does not.

name: QK-norm
what: Normalise queries and keys before the dot product to bound attention logits.

name: DeepNorm
what: Up-weight the residual (α·x) and down-scale initialisation to train 1,000-layer transformers.

name: μP
what: A parametrisation under which the best hyperparameters transfer from small to large widths.

name: z-loss
what: Penalty 10⁻⁴·log²Z keeps the softmax normaliser near 1 (PaLM).

name: Peri-LN
what: Normalise both the input and the output of each sublayer; analyses the 'sandwich' norm open models had adopted.

name: DyT
what: Replace normalisation layers with tanh(αx): transformers without normalisation.

name: QK-Clip / MuonClip
what: Rescale Wq and Wk when a head's maximum logit exceeds a threshold; trained Kimi K2 on 15.5T tokens with no loss spikes.

name: mHC
what: Widen the residual stream to n parallel copies mixed by a doubly stochastic matrix (Sinkhorn–Knopp), keeping the identity path.

name: GELU
what: x·Φ(x): a smooth ReLU.

name: SwiGLU
what: Gated feed-forward (Swish(xW) ⊙ xV)W₂ with d_ff cut by ⅔ to keep parameters equal.
used: PaLM, LLaMA and nearly every LLM since

name: Sparse Transformer
what: Factorised strided and fixed sparse attention patterns.

name: Reformer
what: Locality-sensitive hashing to attend only within hash buckets; reversible layers.

name: Longformer
what: Sliding window plus a few global tokens.

name: Linformer
what: Project keys and values to a fixed length k along the sequence: O(Tk).

name: Linear attention
what: Replace softmax with φ(q)·φ(k); causal attention becomes an RNN with a d×d state.

name: BigBird
what: Window, global and random attention; provably universal.

name: Performer
what: Random features that approximate the softmax kernel (FAVOR+).

name: FlashAttention
what: Exact attention computed in tiles in fast on-chip memory; never stores the T×T matrix.

name: Sliding window (Mistral 7B)
what: Window W = 4,096 per layer; stacked layers reach far further; rolling KV buffer.
used: Mistral; local layers of Gemma 3/4 and gpt-oss

name: Gated DeltaNet
what: Linear attention whose state is updated by a gated delta rule.

name: Native Sparse Attention
what: Trainable sparse attention: compressed, selected and sliding branches, built for GPU kernels.

name: MoBA
what: Mixture-of-experts-style routing of each query to the top-k blocks of keys.

name: DeepSeek Sparse Attention
what: A cheap FP8 'lightning indexer' scores past tokens; each query attends to only the top 2,048.

name: Kimi Linear
what: Kimi Delta Attention layers with one MLA layer in four; up to 75% less KV cache at 1M tokens.

name: MQA
what: All query heads share one key and one value head.

name: PagedAttention
what: Store the KV cache in fixed-size pages, like virtual memory, so batches share memory without fragmentation.

name: Attention sinks
what: Keeping the first tokens' keys and values lets window attention run on endless streams.
used: Streaming inference; learned sinks in gpt-oss

name: Ring attention
what: Split the sequence across devices in a ring, passing key–value blocks round while computing.

name: GQA
what: Groups of query heads share a key–value head: between MHA and MQA.
used: Llama 2 70B, Llama 3, Mistral, Qwen3, gpt-oss, Gemma

name: MLA
what: Cache one 512-dim latent (plus a 64-dim RoPE key) per token instead of per-head keys and values.

name: KV quantisation (KIVI)
what: Store keys and values in 2 bits.

name: Sparsely-gated MoE
what: Noisy top-k gating over many expert networks between LSTM layers.

name: GShard
what: Mixture-of-experts transformer layers sharded across thousands of devices.

name: Switch Transformer
what: Top-1 routing, a capacity factor and a load-balancing loss α·N·Σ fᵢPᵢ.

name: Mixtral 8x7B
what: 8 SwiGLU experts, top-2 routing: 47B parameters, 13B active per token.

name: DeepSeekMoE
what: Many fine-grained experts plus always-on shared experts.

name: Aux-loss-free balancing
what: A per-expert bias added to routing scores before top-k, adjusted by load: balance without a loss term.

name: Engram
what: Hashed n-gram memory lookup as a second axis of sparsity alongside experts.

name: Kaplan scaling laws
what: Loss falls as a power law in parameters, data and compute.

name: Chinchilla
what: Scale parameters and data equally; about 20 tokens per parameter at the optimum.

name: Beyond Chinchilla
what: Counting inference cost, train smaller models on far more tokens.

name: Speculative decoding
what: A small model drafts several tokens; the large model checks them in one pass; rejection sampling keeps the output exact.

name: Medusa
what: Extra prediction heads on the model itself draft the next few tokens.

name: EAGLE
what: Draft at the level of hidden features rather than tokens.

name: Multi-token prediction
what: Train extra heads to predict several future tokens; better code models and self-speculation.

name: S4
what: Structured state-space model for long sequences.

name: RWKV
what: An RNN with transformer-style parallel training.

name: RetNet
what: Retention: parallel, recurrent and chunked forms of one decaying attention.

name: Mamba
what: Selective state-space model: input-dependent state transitions, linear time.

name: Griffin
what: Gated linear recurrence mixed with local attention.

name: Jamba
what: One attention layer in eight, the rest Mamba, with mixture of experts.

name: Mamba-2 / SSD
what: State-space duality: selective SSMs as a form of masked linear attention.

name: Granite 4.0-H
what: Nine Mamba-2 layers to one attention layer, no position encoding.

name: ViT
what: Images as sequences of 16×16 patches through a plain transformer encoder.

name: CLIP
what: Contrastive image–text pre-training of two encoders.

name: Flamingo
what: Perceiver resampler and gated cross-attention feed images into a frozen language model.

name: LLaDA
what: A masked-diffusion language model trained from scratch.

name: Universal Transformer
what: One layer applied repeatedly, with adaptive depth.

name: Parallel attention and FFN
what: x + Attn(LN(x)) + MLP(LN(x)): about 15% faster training (PaLM).

name: Mixture-of-Depths
what: Route only the top-k tokens through each block.

name: Differential Transformer
what: Attention as the difference of two softmax maps, cancelling noise.

name: Byte Latent Transformer
what: No tokeniser: bytes grouped into patches by the entropy of the next byte.

name: Gated attention
what: A sigmoid gate on each head's output; removes attention sinks.
